en: to throb; to palpitate; to beat

examples.en: My heart always pounds before an interview.
My heart raced the night before the trip.

examples.ko: 그 사람을 보면 두근두근하는 마음을 숨길 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can't hide how my heart pounds when I see him.

examples.ko: 내일 결과를 기다릴 때도 가슴이 두근두근할 거예요.
examples.en: My heart will be pounding tomorrow too while I wait for the results.
My heart was pounding and my hands got sweaty.
My heart is racing, so I can't sleep.

explain: '가슴이 두근두근하다'처럼 주어는 보통 '가슴'이나 '마음'이에요. '두근거리다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요. 설렘과 긴장 둘 다 되지만, 무서워서 뛸 때는 '쿵쾅거리다'나 '떨리다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: My heart is pounding, so I can't sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두근두근하다와 같은 뜻이고, 일상 대화에서 더 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 두근두근하다 and heard more often in daily talk.

phrases.en: I opened the letter with a pounding heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -는 lets it describe the noun that follows.

phrases.en: My heart races when I see the person I like.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두근두근하다와 비슷하지만 더 짧고 기본적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 두근두근하다 but shorter and more basic.

explain_en: The subject is usually 가슴 (chest) or 마음 (heart), as in 가슴이 두근두근하다. 두근거리다 means the same. It covers both excitement and nerves; for fear, 쿵쾅거리다 or 떨리다 sounds more natural.

examples.en: The child suddenly screamed at the top of his voice.
He got angry and snapped back fiercely.
My younger sister cried, screaming her lungs out.
No matter how I coax him, he just keeps insisting fiercely.

examples.ko: 엄마한테 바락 화를 내고 나서 후회했어요.
examples.en: I lashed out at my mom and then regretted it.
It felt so unfair that I shouted out before I knew it.

explain: 갑자기 크게 소리 지르거나 대들 때 쓰는 말이에요. '바락 소리를 지르다, 바락 대들다, 바락 악을 쓰다'처럼 말해요. 같은 말을 반복한 '바락바락'도 써요.

phrases.example: 동생이 갑자기 바락 소리를 질러서 놀랐어요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling suddenly shouted, and I was startled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 크게 소리칠 때 가장 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for suddenly shouting loudly.

phrases.en: The child talked back fiercely to the mother.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화가 나서 윗사람에게 거세게 맞서는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes angrily talking back to someone, especially an elder.

phrases.example: 그는 바락바락 악을 쓰며 화를 냈어요.
phrases.en: He yelled at the top of his lungs in anger.
phrases.nuance_ko: '바락'을 반복해서 소리를 계속 지르는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The repeated form for shouting again and again.

explain_en: It describes suddenly shouting or lashing out. Typical phrases are '바락 소리를 지르다', '바락 대들다' and '바락 악을 쓰다'. The repeated form '바락바락' is also used.

examples.en: The door suddenly opened and I was startled.
I flinched when I heard a noise behind me on the night road.
My sibling woke from a dream and sat up with a start.

examples.ko: 그는 전화벨 소리에 소스라쳐서 컵을 떨어뜨렸어요.
examples.en: He was so startled by the phone ringing that he dropped his cup.
I almost jumped out of my skin when I saw a snake at my feet.
My friend flinched as if startled.

explain: 주로 '소스라치게 놀라다' 꼴로 써요. '깜짝 놀라다'보다 몸이 움찔할 만큼 크게 놀랄 때 어울려요. 활용은 소스라쳐요, 소스라쳤어요예요.

phrases.example: 갑자기 큰 소리가 나서 소스라치게 놀랐어요.
phrases.en: A loud noise came suddenly and I was badly startled.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소스라치다'를 가장 자주 쓰는 꼴로, 몸이 움찔할 만큼 크게 놀랄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form of 소스라치다, used when you are startled enough to flinch.

phrases.en: I was startled by the thunder and woke up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀란 이유를 이어서 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form used to link the reason for being startled.

phrases.en: The lights suddenly went out and I was startled.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소스라치다'보다 쉽고 일상에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 소스라치다 and more common in everyday speech.

explain_en: It is mostly used in the form '소스라치게 놀라다'. Compared with '깜짝 놀라다', it fits a shock big enough to make your body flinch. The conjugations are 소스라쳐요 and 소스라쳤어요.

examples.ko: 동생이 장난감을 못 사게 되자 심통이 났어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling got sulky when he couldn't get the toy.
Why is your little brother acting spiteful since this morning?
My older brother is so cranky that we often fight.
He is sitting there with a sulky face.

examples.ko: 괜히 심통 부리지 말고 말로 해요.
examples.en: Don't throw a tantrum for nothing, just say it in words.
He acted spiteful and ended up getting scolded.

explain: '심통이 나다'는 마음에 안 들어 기분이 상했을 때, '심통을 부리다'는 일부러 투정이나 못된 짓을 할 때 써요. 아이나 가까운 사이에 잘 어울리고, '심술'과 비슷한 짝으로 쓰는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: My little brother is being spiteful today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '심통'과 비슷한 말이고 짝으로 자주 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A close word to 심통 that often pairs with it.

phrases.en: He is sitting there with a sulky face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기분이 상해서 뚱한 표정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a sulky, displeased expression.

phrases.en: Please don't act mean to your friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부러 못되게 구는 사람에게 그만하라고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to tell someone to stop being deliberately mean.

explain_en: '심통이 나다' is used when you are upset because something is not to your liking, and '심통을 부리다' when you deliberately act spiteful or throw a fit. It suits children or close relationships, and often pairs much like '심술'.

examples.ko: 그는 학벌에 대한 열등의식이 있다고 해요.
examples.en: They say he has a sense of inferiority about his educational background.

examples.ko: 열등의식은 남과 비교할 때 더 커져요.
examples.en: A sense of inferiority grows bigger when you compare yourself with others.
I started working out to get free of my sense of inferiority.

examples.ko: 열등의식 때문에 사람들 앞에서 말하기가 힘들어요.
examples.en: Because of my feelings of inferiority, it's hard to speak in front of people.

examples.ko: 아이에게 열등의식을 심어 주면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't plant a sense of inferiority in a child.

examples.ko: 열등의식도 잘 쓰면 노력하는 힘이 돼요.
examples.en: Even a sense of inferiority can become a driving force if used well.

explain: 일상에서는 '열등감'이 더 자주 들리고, 열등의식은 설명하거나 글로 쓸 때 어울려요. 반대 느낌의 말은 '우월감'이에요. '콤플렉스가 있다'도 비슷한 뜻으로 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: I feel inferior when I compare myself to my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 남보다 못하다고 느낄 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when one feels inferior to others.
phrases.en_equiv: to feel a sense of inferiority

phrases.en: He suffered from a sense of inferiority for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그런 마음 때문에 오래 힘들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when that feeling troubles someone for a long time.
phrases.en_equiv: to be tormented by a sense of inferiority

phrases.en: I lack confidence because of my feelings of inferiority.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '열등의식'보다 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common than 열등의식 in everyday conversation.

explain_en: In everyday speech '열등감' is heard more often; 열등의식 suits explanations and writing. The opposite feeling is '우월감'. Koreans also say '콤플렉스가 있다' with a similar meaning.

examples.en: After being treated unfairly, I was filled with pent-up anger.
I went to karaoke to let out the anger inside me.
After holding it in for so long, my anger built up.
My chest feels tight because of suppressed anger.
The boss couldn't hold back his anger and shouted.

examples.ko: 울화에 찬 얼굴로 그가 방에서 나왔어요.
examples.en: He came out of the room with a face full of rage.

explain: 바로 터지는 '화'와 달리 속에 참고 눌러서 쌓인 화를 말해요. '울화가 치밀다', '울화가 쌓이다', '울화를 풀다'처럼 짝말로 자주 써요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '화가 나다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I just kept holding it in, and the pent-up anger piled up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화를 풀지 못하고 계속 마음에 쌓일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when anger isn't released and keeps building up inside.

phrases.en: I'm furious when I hear that news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쌓인 화가 한꺼번에 폭발하는 느낌이고 구어에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels like built-up anger bursting out; common in speech.

phrases.en: I calmed my pent-up anger with a walk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화를 터뜨리지 않고 천천히 가라앉힐 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when calming anger slowly without letting it explode.

explain_en: Unlike '화' that flares up right away, it means anger that has been held in and piled up inside. It often appears in collocations such as '울화가 치밀다', '울화가 쌓이다' and '울화를 풀다'. In daily talk people also just say '화가 나다'.

examples.en: It was my first presentation, so the pressure was huge.
I took deep breaths to overcome the pressure.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 결승전의 중압감 속에서도 침착했어요.
examples.en: That player stayed calm even under the pressure of the final.

examples.ko: 부모님의 기대가 중압감으로 느껴질 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes my parents' expectations feel like a heavy burden.

examples.ko: 중압감 때문에 밤에 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: Because of the pressure, I can't sleep at night.
I'm always weighed down by pressure before exams.

explain: '스트레스'보다 마음을 무겁게 짓누르는 느낌이 강해요. 시험, 결승전, 큰 책임처럼 잘해야 한다는 부담 앞에서 써요. 보통 '중압감을 느끼다', '중압감에 시달리다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: I felt pressure before the big match.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이 무겁게 눌리는 느낌이 들 때 쓰는 기본 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic collocation for feeling mentally weighed down.

phrases.en: He suffers from pressure because of his responsibilities.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부담이 오래 계속되어 힘들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the pressure continues for a long time and is tough.

phrases.en: I can't sleep because of the pressure.
phrases.nuance_ko: '중압감'보다 약하고 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Milder than 중압감 and more common in daily life.

explain_en: It feels more crushing than '스트레스', like a weight pressing on your mind. It is used when facing the burden of needing to do well, such as exams, finals or big responsibilities. Common patterns are '중압감을 느끼다' and '중압감에 시달리다'.
